episodes.title: Likeability Expert: Stop Doing This, It’s Why People Quietly Avoid You! | Vanessa Van Edwards
episodes.summary: 20 points taken verbatim from The Diary Of A CEO, spanning 6:16–2:18:45. Selected from the transcript by information density — every line below is what was said, not a description of it.

learnings.headline: It's actually just because you probably haven't learned the mechanics of conversation.
learnings.detail: It's actually just because you probably haven't learned the mechanics of conversation.
learnings.passage: You feel overwhelmed when you're in conversation. So if you're in conversation and you're social overthinking, you cannot turn your brain off. All you're worried about is what you're going to say next. It's actually just because you probably haven't learned the mechanics of conversation. There's a blueprint to good conversation. We're going to talk about it. Once you know the blueprint, it becomes easier. And the last symptom of bad conversation is that you leave feeling misunderstood. You leave feeling like I was the worst version of myself or I wasn't able to be my best self. I think really good conversationalists, people leave conversation with them thinking, wow, after talking to you, I feel like I understand myself better.
learnings.evidence: It's actually just because you probably haven't learned the mechanics of conversation.

I wasn't quite sure what they were, but I could see that very good conversationalists, they were following some kind of plan. Okay. Then eight years ago, this is when the real research began, and it started with an experiment. I call it my speed networking experiment. This fundamentally changed the way I think about conversations. Here's what we did.
learnings.evidence: So accidentally, I've been doing research for this my whole life because I was very bad at conversation for 20 years.

learnings.headline: I realized, wow, conversation now is not just about a way for me to make friends.
learnings.detail: And I realized, wow, conversation now is not just about a way for me to make friends.
learnings.passage: And I was, like, excited. I was like, okay, I'm going to meet more moms. Here we go. And I walk in the room and everyone's... scrolling, everyone's on their feed. And I realized, wow, conversation now is not just about a way for me to make friends. It actually has to compete with that feed. I have to make my questions and my answers so dopamine worthy that they're actually going to beat that feed. Otherwise, they're going to go right back to their phone. That is why these have to do more lifting. Because if I want to compete with the feed, I have to produce dopamine, a little bit of excitement, a little bit of motivation. I also have to create what I would call, forgive me for this word, but conversational confetti. This is like we got to lift a little bit more in our conversations because otherwise someone's going to go right back to scrolling.
learnings.evidence: And I realized, wow, conversation now is not just about a way for me to make friends.
